vram.title: S-OS Memory & AI Infrastructure™
vram.subtitle: From $1.50 microcontrollers to Embedded Linux (Yocto/Ubuntu/Alpine) devices and $30,000 GPU AI servers. Eliminating memory limits and extending Flash/eMMC lifespan.
vram.productEdgeDesc: For ESP32, STM32, RP2040, Yocto Linux, Ubuntu, Alpine, and Raspberry Pi. Extends SRAM up to 43x and protects eMMC/Flash storage wear by 10x–40x.
vram.productGpuDesc: For PCs, AI workstations, and LLM servers. Enables running 70B+ LLM models on standard consumer GPUs with compressed PCIe Tensor Offloading and CUDA Cosine Resonance.
vram.esp32Desc: Pure C++11 for ESP32, STM32, RP2040, and PIC32. Tested on 8.0MB+ V-RAM with 0 errors, 147 KB/s write speed, and 43.54x compression.
vram.linuxDesc: Native C++11 POSIX support for Yocto Linux (Poky), Ubuntu, Alpine, and Raspberry Pi. Supports zero-code LD_PRELOAD integration and reduces eMMC/Flash write wear by 10x–40x.
vram.gpuDesc: Native CUDA C++ integration for NVIDIA RTX 3090/4090/H100. Accelerated vector search and Tensor Paging.
vram.matrixSubtitle: Select the optimal vram(blockSize, ramLimit, maxBlocks) parameters for your embedded application or Linux OS:
vram.modeDensityUse: Dataloggers, smart meters, dense databases, telemetry.
vram.modeCriticalUse: Time-critical robotics (LIDAR, autonomous navigation), real-time AI, framebuffers.
vram.modeMassiveUse: Yocto/Ubuntu Linux gateways, eMMC wear reduction, large neural network weights.
vram.modeMicroUse: Sub-$1 MCUs, minimal heap environments, basic event counters.
vram.codeTitle: Simple C++ API for Integration (MCU & POSIX Linux)
vram.communityDesc: Max 512 KB V-RAM. Permanently free for prototypes, evaluation, and non-commercial open-source projects.
vram.proDesc: Unlocked V-RAM (up to 16MB–50MB+). Perpetual license for 1 product + 12 months of free updates and email support.
vram.growthDesc: Unlocked V-RAM (up to 16MB–50MB+). Perpetual license for fast-growing series + 12 months of support.
vram.enterpriseDesc: Royalty per unit (or $15,000/year). For Embedded Linux gateways and V-RAM GPU/AI workstations. Includes Source Code Escrow and SLA.
vram.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions About V-RAM Engine
vram.faq1Q: Is the license a one-time payment or does it renew every year?
vram.faq1A: The Commercial Pro ($299) and Growth ($1,499) licenses are perpetual. They are paid as a one-time fee and grant you lifetime manufacturing rights for your device. The software in your devices never expires.
vram.faq2Q: What compression ratio can I expect on my real-world data?
vram.faq2A: The 43.54x ratio is a V-RAM Peak achieved during boundary stress testing on synthetic repeating patterns. For real-world CAN-bus vehicle telemetry, sensor logs, and neural network weights (AI weights), typical real-world compression ranges from 3x to 8x, which still reduces Flash/eMMC storage usage and wear by over 75%.
vram.faq3Q: Does V-RAM support Embedded Linux (Yocto, Ubuntu, Alpine)?
vram.faq3A: Yes! V-RAM is written in pure ANSI C++11 (POSIX) and runs natively on Yocto Linux (Poky), Ubuntu, Alpine, and Raspberry Pi. Beyond the clean C++ API, it supports zero-code 'LD_PRELOAD' shared library injection for legacy Linux binaries.
vram.faq4Q: What happens if I manufacture more devices than the license threshold allows?
vram.faq4A: Production thresholds (Volume Caps) protect smaller startups and inventors. If your production exceeds 2,000 units per year, you simply pay the difference to upgrade to Commercial Growth or switch to the Enterprise OEM Royalty model ($0.15 per unit).
